podcast.title: Basketball Player Name
podcast.body: This was the original name of the band that would later become Pearl Jam. The name was adopted in homage to one of their favorite basketball players before they signed with Epic Records and officially changed their name. "went by the name Mookie Blaylock, named after one of their favorite basketball players."

podcast.title: Predecessor to Pearl Jam
podcast.body: This band was the initial name for the group that would later become Pearl Jam. They went into the studio and created a "proper demo" of the song "Alive" (then called "Dollar Short"), which successfully secured them a record deal. "The new band was called Mookie Blaylock and they went into the studio and by this time Dollar Short had been renamed Alive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Predecessor to Pearl Jam – Formation with Eddie Vedder
podcast.body: Mookie Blaylock was the original name of the band formed by Mother Love Bone's Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard, who invited a young singer named Eddie Vedder from San Diego to join. The band quickly changed its name to Pearl Jam, which went on to achieve massive success. "This kid from San Diego who had just flown up at the invitation of Jeff and Stone to sing in a new band that was going to be called Mookie Blaylock, and that kid's name was Eddie Vedder."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Securing a Record Deal
podcast.body: The band Mookie Blaylock secured a record deal based on a proper demo of the song "Alive," which was then still known as "Dollar Short." "Well that worked out pretty well and Mookie Blaylock found themselves with a record deal."

xref.title: Initial Lack of Attention, Later Multi-Platinum Success – Post-Hype Phenomenon
xref.body: Despite receiving great reviews upon its release in April 1991, the Temple of the Dog album was largely ignored by the public. However, once Mookie Blaylock changed its name to Pearl Jam and both Soundgarden and Pearl Jam achieved massive global success, interest in the album exploded, leading it to sell multi-platinum worldwide. "It got great reviews, but nobody paid much attention until Mookie Blaylock changed their name to Pearl Jam and, well, you know, that story."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Temple of the Dog Rise – Boosts Prior Project
xref.body: After Mookie Blaylock changed their name to Pearl Jam and the band "blew up," their success retrospectively drew massive attention to the Temple of the Dog album, which had initially been ignored. This surge in popularity led the Temple of the Dog record to achieve multi-platinum sales worldwide. "But when Soundgarden and Pearl Jam blew up, the record went multi-platinum all over the world."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Transformation into Pearl Jam – Post-Tragedy Rebirth
xref.body: Following the tragic death of Andrew Wood, the surviving members of Mother Love Bone, Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard, collaborated with Chris Cornell and Matt Cameron to form Temple of the Dog. This collaboration eventually led Ament and Gossard to form a new band with Eddie Vedder, initially called Mookie Blaylock, which soon became Pearl Jam. "When Mother Lovebone collapsed and turned into Pearl Jam, Kelly became their full-time manager, leaving Susan to deal with Allison Chains."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
